text:
alex (Cloud Partnerships): Heads up — NetShift (SI partner) asked if they can stack our marketplace promo credits on top of a private-offer commit for customer X. they want to show a bigger discount to close this quarter.

devin (Sales): they pushed this as 'must-have' on the deal. customer X is a 12mo commit, $900k ARR. close this week would hit quota.

liam (Finance): stacking marketplace credits + private offer discounts is usually additive risk. need to see net revenue/recognition impact. what's the ask exactly?

alex (Cloud Partnerships): proposal: 20% private-offer discount + marketplace promo credit equivalent to 10% in first 3 months (apply as credits). Net effective ~28% after rounding. SI wants partner margin split 60/40.

maria (Partnerships Ops): quick note — marketplace credits have program limits. we can do short-term promotional credits but we need SKU mapping and an SOW that shows credits consumed.

sam (SI Partner Lead): NetShift says they'll take 60% margin on the delta to run the PoC and integration. we told them partner margin guidelines are flexible if there's product-led expansion potential.

nora (Legal): need to avoid creating contingent rebates that hurt revenue deferral. if credits are applied as a post-bill credit, that's one thing; if they're structured as an up-front discount in the private offer that reduces invoice amount, that's revenue reduction. both OK but different accounting.

liam (Finance): can we model two variants? (A) credits applied as separate marketplace credit line (no revenue deferral beyond customer acceptance) (B) reduce contract value in private offer. I think (A) preserves higher recognized revenue earlier.

devin (Sales): customer prefers visibility on invoice = lower invoice helps procurement. they might not accept credits applied after invoicing.

maria (Partnerships Ops): pragmatic approach: do a hybrid. private offer reflects committed spend (full $900k), marketplace credits issued as promotional resource that must be redeemed in product within 90 days. that keeps invoice intact but delivers budget relief.

alex (Cloud Partnerships): good. how do we show that to partner and legal? can we give a simple T&Cs snippet?

nora (Legal): draft snippet — short form: "Marketplace promotional credits are granted separately from the private offer. They are consumable product credits, non-refundable, and do not alter the private-offer invoiced commitment. Redemption terms: 90 days, subject to standard marketplace credit policy."

sam (SI Partner Lead): NetShift will want the credits to apply to implementation fees too — they bill through our marketplace integration. is that allowed?

liam (Finance): marketplace credits can be restricted to product SKUs only. we should avoid credits covering partner professional services unless explicitly allowed. that's a can of worms for revenue sharing.

devin (Sales): customer X wants partner services included in the first-phase scope. can we offer a small PS voucher from Redwood (not marketplace credit) and let partner keep margin? say $25k voucher?

alex (Cloud Partnerships): proposal: 10% marketplace promo credit (product-only, 90d), $25k Redwood PS voucher (redeemable with NetShift) and 20% private-offer discount on committed list. partner margin split 60/40 on the private-offer residual.

maria (Partnerships Ops): ops checklist: need marketplace SKU list, promo code creation, voucher contract, private-offer JSON, and partner payout setup. timeline to deliver all pieces = 48 hrs if Legal signs off.

nora (Legal): I'll draft the credit T&Cs and a short partner addendum that disallows credits on PS unless voucher used. will ping for review by EOD.

liam (Finance): run a P&L quick: worst-case revenue impact with credits + voucher = ~7% hit in recognized revenue first quarter, still within deal economics given 12mo term. confirm if partner payout is on invoiced amount or net after voucher?

alex (Cloud Partnerships): partner payout will be on committed net after private-offer discount but before Redwood PS voucher. re-checkable.

devin (Sales): I'm going to loop in procurement and the customer's legal — want to get acceptance today. I'll also flag the marketability: we should reuse this playbook for other SI-led enterprise closes if it works.

partnerships-bot: marketplace-promo created: promo_id=mp-2026-331, 10% product credit, expires in 90 days. (automated message)

maria (Partnerships Ops): action items: @nora finalize T&Cs, @liam confirm revenue treatment for voucher, @alex send partner addendum to NetShift, @devin share package with customer. target: sign by EOW.

sam (SI Partner Lead): NetShift appreciative. will push for acceptance and confirm margin split. updating internal pricing sheet now. :thumbsup:

alex (Cloud Partnerships): thanks all. small ask — capture this as a reusable template in the partner playbook if EOW closes. I'll add a note in Confluence after legal approves.

devin (Sales): if this closes we'll mark as 'marketplace-credit + voucher' play variant in deal desk.

maria (Partnerships Ops): noted. keeping thread open for updates.
